# Staying honest against the ecosystem: this archive's test module (and only
# this one) requires datastar-go, the wire-conformance reference. The Go test
# emits the same element and signal events through the generated handler and
# through datastar.NewSSE and compares the two bodies byte for byte.

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=Server
muxt check

exec go mod tidy
exec go test -count=1

-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /stream datastar(sse(Mixed(ctx, send, marshalJSON(sendSignals))))" -}}
{{- with .Selector "#list" -}}{{- end -}}
{{- with .Mode "append" -}}{{- end -}}
<li>{{ .Result }}</li>
{{- end -}}
-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24

require github.com/starfederation/datastar-go v1.2.2
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type Sig struct {
	Count int `json:"count"`
}

type Server struct{}

func (Server) Mixed(_ context.Context, send func(string) error, sendSignals func(Sig) error) {
	_ = send("one")
	_ = sendSignals(Sig{Count: 1})
}
-- template_test.go --
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/starfederation/datastar-go/datastar"
)

func Test(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	TemplateRoutes(mux, Server{})

	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/stream", nil)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)

	sdkRec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	sdkReq := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/stream", nil)
	sse := datastar.NewSSE(sdkRec, sdkReq)
	if err := sse.PatchElements("<li>one</li>", datastar.WithSelector("#list"), datastar.WithModeAppend()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := sse.MarshalAndPatchSignals(Sig{Count: 1}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	if got, want := rec.Body.String(), sdkRec.Body.String(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("generated handler body and datastar-go body differ\ngenerated: %q\nsdk:       %q", got, want)
	}
}
